title: WPSS/1372/2007 of SMT. JANKI DEVI NAUTIYAL Vs STATE and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No.1372 of 2007
Smt. Janki Devi Nautiyal ÖÖ..ÖPetitioner
Versus
State of U.P. and others Ö.ÖRespondents

Present: Mr. Pankaj Purohit, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
 Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder present for the State of
Uttarakhand.
 Ms. Beena Pandey, Standing Counsel present for the
State of U.P.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The husband of the petitioner was appointed as
Assistant Teacher (L.T. Grade) on 31.12.1977. Pursuant to
the order dated 31.12.1977, he joined the post of Assistant
Teacher (L.T. Grade) only on 09.01.1978 and in less than a
month he passed away on 02.02.1978. Thereafter, all these
years the petitioner kept quiet and after more than 25
years now claims family pension for herself by means of the
present writ petition.
2. Not only the writ petition is hopelessly barred by
time but the learned counsel representing the State of U.P.
Ms. Beena Pandey has apprised this Court that at the time
when husband of the petitioner was in service in the year
1978 in order to be entitled for the family pension, the
husband of the petitioner must have put in at least one
yearís of service, as per the pension rules prevalent at that
time. This condition is also contained in the letter dated
24.08.1996 of the Deputy Secretary to the Government of
U.P. issued to various departments, which is made part of
record, which clearly states that such a family pension will
be given to the dependents of a government servant who
have put in one yearís continuous service.

2
3. According to the petitioner, this condition was
relaxed later on by the Government on 21.09.1979. But
since this was not done retrospectively, in the event, this
condition was relaxed, it is not applicable in the case of the
petitioner.
4. In view thereof, the writ petition is devoid of any
merit. It is hereby dismissed. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 01.07.2014
